land.text: Egypt, from which Amyrtaeus expelled the Persians (Memphis in 405)
Egypt, taken by Nefaarud I of Mendes in 398

rulers.name: Amyrtaeus (Amenirdis)
rulers.note: The page: the dynasty "includes only one Pharaoh".

correction.text: Egypt, "detached from Persian administration" under Amyrtaeus; the page gives no territory

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; the 28th page says nothing of territory ("very little is known" about the reign) and names only Sais and Memphis. The whole valley is drawn at low confidence; the 27th page notes Artaxerxes II was still recognised in parts of Egypt as late as 401, which is not drawn. No area.

region.text: Egypt, the whole Nile Valley and Delta

ledger.note: 404: Amyrtaeus proclaims himself Pharaoh of Egypt after Darius II's death, having expelled the Persians from Memphis in 405 BC (page: "proclaimed himself Pharaoh of Egypt"; "succeeded in expelling the Persians from Memphis in 405 BC"). The land is the researcher's reading.

398: Nefaarud I of Mendes overthrows Amyrtaeus. The 29th page says he defeated Amyrtaeus "in open battle, and later putting him to death at Memphis"; the 28th page infobox: "Deposition of Amyrtaeus: 398 BC".
398: the Twenty-eighth Dynasty ends with the deposition and execution of Amyrtaeus; the page says it "lasted from 404 BC to 398 BC".

wars.name: Nefaarud I's rising against Amyrtaeus
wars.outcome: Nefaarud I defeated Amyrtaeus in open battle and put him to death at Memphis; the page gives no campaign years.
wars.note: Years -399..-398 are the researcher's bracket around the 398 date.

notes: A six-year dynasty with one pharaoh, below the ten-year bar but named as predecessor of the Twenty-ninth by me-03-c and as successor of the Persian dynasty; written minimally from two pages. The page says very little is known; its territory is therefore drawn as the whole valley at confidence 2 and the Memphis expulsion of 405 is recorded in the 27th dossier. The body of the 27th page dates the rebellion from 411.
